newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Netanyahu delays cabinet shake-up.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Netanyahu delays cabinet shake-up.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has delayed an anticipated cabinet reshuffle until next week, his spokesman said on Wednesday.

"The appointments are not yet closed," the spokesman Shai Bazak told Israel radio. "It will be presented to the Knesset (parliament) only at the start of the week. I imagine it will be finished in coming days."

Analysts said the delay stemmed from a dispute between Netanyahu and Foreign Minister David Levy over the possible inclusion of ultra-hawk Ariel Sharon in the Israeli leader's team of insiders who hammer out strategy in Arab-Israeli negotiations.
Infrastructure Minister Sharon, who is poised to be named finance minister, has demanded he be included in the inner cabinet that now comprises Netanyahu, Levy and Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai.
The delay came hours after the Israeli government defeated a parliamentary no-confidence motion Tuesday night -- but without support from 11 of 66 coalition members, including Levy.
Israeli media reports said Levy, a relative moderate in Netanyahu's rightist-religious government, had threatened to resign if Sharon got into the inner cabinet.
Levy and four other lawmakers of his Gesher faction that is allied to Netanyahu's ruling Likud party abstained or absented themselves from Tuesday's no-confidence vote.
"I am sure things will be worked out," Bazak told the radio.

Tourism Minister Moshe Katzav is expected to be named infrastructure minister when Sharon is shifted to the Treasury. The tourism and science portfolios are expected to be filled respectively by Likud lawmakers Silvan Shalom and Michael Eitan.
